structured_output.world_model: W2 empirical, after E027. Tip E027: 5.878 s, 0.7547 on seeds 0-2. Held-out mean is about 0.7526, so the bar is a coin flip. Time is predictable from pixel count and step count: about 5% per 0.5 epoch. Accuracy changes under 0.4 pp are unreadable on 3 seeds. Every time-neutral recipe tweak measured so far (wd, LS, Muon lr, EMA exponent, LR floor) was flat within noise. So the I047, I048, I049 and I051 forecasts sit at the tip's accuracy with a ±0.25 pp range, and time stays at about 5.88 s. The one exception is I050, which removes real compute by moving steps from 24 px to 20 px.

forecasts.reason: LR timing tweaks have been flat in the table; the step count is unchanged, so the RNG stream may shift but the mean stays about the same.
The averaging knob has been flat or slightly negative; the interval change is time-neutral and unlikely to give +0.15 pp.
LS has been flat (E013); a two-stage change adds little and risks a small cost from the GPU scalar.
20 px steps are cheaper than 24 px, saving about 2.5%, but E011 and E018 show that low-res steps cost some accuracy, so the held-out mean likely falls below 0.752.
Per-resolution whitening is a never-measured mechanism with extra prepare cost and eigh calls; any gain is likely within noise.

cruxes: Is the held-out 10-seed mean of the tip really about 0.7526, below the 0.753 bar? If it is, every further trim fails.
Does any time-neutral recipe lever (LR timing, Lookahead interval, LS schedule) move held-out accuracy by 0.15 pp or more? Measured levers so far were flat.
Does moving steps from 24 px to 20 px save at least 2% of time without an accuracy cost?
